annotations.chapterTitle: Appendix I: The Split Among the German Communists

annotation.targetText: We must create a powerful international women's movement, on a clear theoretical basis
annotation.summary: Lenin insists that women's liberation requires an international mass movement grounded in scientific socialist theory.
annotation.explanation: Rather than leaving women's organization to bourgeois charities or spontaneous reformism, Lenin argues the Communist International must build a theoretically rigorous movement of working women.

annotation.targetText: The great social question appears as an adjunct, a part, of sexual problems. The main thing becomes a subsidiary matter. That not only endangers clarity on that question itself, it muddles the thoughts, the class-consciousness of proletarian women generally.
annotation.summary: Treating class struggle as secondary to personal sexual theories confuses working-class consciousness.
annotation.explanation: Lenin warns that isolating sex and marriage from the struggle against capitalist exploitation inverts Marxist priorities and weakens revolutionary focus during acute political crises.

annotation.targetText: No special organisations for women. A woman communist is a member of the Party just as a man communist, with equal rights and duties. There can be no difference of opinion on that score. Nevertheless, we must not close our eyes to the fact that the Party must have bodies, working groups, commissions, committees, bureaus or whatever you like, whose particular duty it is to arouse the masses of women workers
annotation.summary: Equal membership in a single Communist Party combined with specialized Party women's commissions for mass agitation.
annotation.explanation: Lenin balances organizational unity (men and women fighting together in one vanguard party) with practical revolutionary reality (dedicated women's bureaus like the Soviet Zhenotdel to organize working women).

annotation.targetText: The rejection of the necessity for separate bodies for our work among the women masses is a conception allied to those of our highly principled and most radical friends of the Communist Labour Party. According to them there must be only one form of organisation, workers' unions. I know them. Many revolutionary but confused minds appeal to principle 'whenever ideas are lacking'.
annotation.summary: Lenin critiques the ultra-left Communist Labour Party for appealing to abstract 'pure principle' to reject practical organizational work among women.
annotation.explanation: Ultra-left sectarians in the German Communist Labour Party (KAPD) opposed dedicated Party women's commissions in the name of abstract organizational purity, ignoring the concrete material obstacles keeping working women from political life.

annotation.targetText: The women must be made conscious of the political connection between our demands and their own suffering, needs, and wishes. They must realise what the proletarian dictatorship means for them: complete equality with man in law and practice, in the family, in the state, in society; an end to the power of the bourgeoisie.
annotation.summary: Immediate struggles must bridge working women's daily grievances to the necessity of working-class political power.
annotation.explanation: Abstract slogans alone cannot mobilize unorganized women; communists must link concrete economic and social demands to the goal of establishing a workers' state that guarantees full equality.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.targetText: We are also opposed to "Left" phrase-mongering. The thinking of "Leftists" outstrips a given stage of development of the objective process; some regard their fantasies as truth, while others strain to realize in the present an ideal which can only be realized in the future. They alienate themselves from the current practice of the majority of the people and from the realities of the day, and show themselves adventurist in their actions.
annotation.summary: Ultra-leftism detaches revolutionary desires from current material conditions and mass consciousness, mistaking wishful fantasies for immediate reality and leading to reckless adventurism.
annotation.explanation: Mao provides a sharp epistemological diagnosis of ultra-leftism: whereas Right opportunists lag behind objective reality, ultra-leftists detach their subjective desires from the actual material stage of development and the consciousness of the masses, substituting revolutionary-sounding slogans and reckless adventurism for patient mass organization.
annotation.context: Small ultra-left sects that reject united-front coalitions or trade union struggles because those struggles do not immediately abolish capitalism isolate themselves from the working class.

annotations.chapterTitle: On the Relation Between Knowledge and Practice, Between Knowing and Doing

annotation.targetText: Discover the truth through practice, and again through practice verify and develop the truth. Start from perceptual knowledge and actively develop it into rational knowledge; then start from rational knowledge and actively guide revolutionary practice to change both the subjective and the objective world. Practice, knowledge, again practice, and again knowledge.
annotation.summary: Human knowledge develops in an endless upward spiral: starting from practical experience, rising to rational theory, and returning to revolutionary practice to test and deepen truth.
annotation.explanation: Mao's concluding synthesis encapsulates the entire Marxist-Leninist theory of knowledge. Truth is not a static dogma achieved once and for all, but a continuous, upward-spiraling cycle in which practical struggle generates theoretical insight, and theoretical insight guides higher levels of revolutionary practice.
annotation.context: In socialist economic planning and community organizing, policies are formulated from concrete surveys, tested in pilot programs, evaluated against real-world outcomes, and refined for broader implementation.

annotations.chapterTitle: On the Relation Between Knowledge and Practice, Between Knowing and Doing

annotation.targetText: The mobilization of the common people throughout the country will create a vast sea in which to drown the enemy, create the conditions that will make up for our inferiority m arms and other things, and create the prerequisites for overcoming every difficulty in the war.
annotation.summary: Politically mobilizing the broad masses creates a vast human sea that overwhelms the invader and overcomes inferior weaponry.
annotation.explanation: Mao argues that military inferiority in weapons is secondary compared to political mobilization; explaining the political aim of the war and linking it to the daily lives of soldiers and peasants turns the entire population into an active force.
annotation.context: Where the Kuomintang relied on passive conscription and censorship, the Communist-led base areas mobilized peasant, women's, and youth associations into active defense.

annotations.chapterTitle: Political Mobilization for the War of Resistance

annotation.targetText: In the great river of absolute fluidity throughout the war there is relative stability at each particular stretch: such is our fundamental view regarding war plans or policies.
annotation.summary: Although battlefield conditions constantly shift, military and political strategy requires plans that remain relatively stable throughout each specific stage of development.
annotation.explanation: Mao applies the dialectical unity of absolute motion and relative rest to strategic planning, refuting both rigid dogmatists who never adapt plans and relativists who reject planning altogether.
annotation.context: While tactical battle plans changed several times a day, the Eighth Route Army's overarching strategic policy of guerrilla and mobile warfare remained stable throughout an entire phase of the war.

annotation.targetText: The question of decisive engagements in the anti-Japanese war should be approached from three aspects: we should resolutely fight a decisive engagement in every campaign or battle in which we are sure of victory; we should avoid a decisive engagement in every campaign or battle in which we are not sure of victory; and we should absolutely avoid a strategically decisive engagement on which the fate of the whole nation is staked.
annotation.summary: Revolutionary forces should fight decisive battles only when local victory is assured, avoid battles when conditions are unfavorable, and never gamble the fate of the entire nation on a single all-or-nothing showdown.
annotation.explanation: Mao explains the principle of trading space for time: temporarily giving up a city or territory to preserve the main armed forces prevents the invader from winning a quick decision and ensures the survival of the resistance.
annotation.context: When Kuomintang commanders rashly staked elite divisions in static positional battles early in the war, they suffered catastrophic losses, whereas mobile withdrawals preserved forces for protracted resistance.

annotations.chapterTitle: The Question of Decisive Engagements in the Anti-Japanese War

annotation.targetText: The only way to settle questions of an ideological nature or controversial issues among the people is by the democratic method, the method of discussion, criticism, persuasion and education, and not by the method of coercion or repression.
annotation.summary: Ideological questions and debates among the people cannot be solved by force or administrative bans; they can only be resolved through open discussion, criticism, persuasion, and education.
annotation.explanation: Because ideological beliefs and questions of right and wrong among the people cannot be forced by decree, Mao insists on patient reasoning, debate, and the 'unity : criticism : unity' method.
annotation.context: Banning a mistaken viewpoint among workers without explaining why it is wrong only drives the idea underground, whereas open discussion builds genuine understanding.

annotations.bookTitle: On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People
annotations.chapterTitle: On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People

annotation.targetText: Revisionism, or Right opportunism, is a bourgeois trend of thought that is even more dangerous than dogmatism.
annotation.summary: Revisionism is a bourgeois ideological trend inside the socialist movement that is even more dangerous than dogmatism because it hollows out the core of Marxism from within.
annotation.explanation: Mao warns that while dogmatists apply Marxist phrases mechanically, revisionists pay lip-service to Marxism while attacking its core principles: materialist dialectics, party leadership, and the people's democratic dictatorship.
annotation.context: Political factions that use socialist rhetoric while dismantling public ownership and weakening working-class state power pave the way for capitalist restoration.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.targetText: In all probability, the proletarian revolution will transform existing society gradually and will be able to abolish private property only when the means of production are available in sufficient quantity.
annotation.summary: Social transformation requires a transition period to develop collective production facilities and reorganize social administration.

annotations.chapterTitle: 17. Will It Be Possible for Private Property to Be Abolished at One Stroke?

annotation.targetText: No, no more than existing forces of production can at one stroke be multiplied to the extent necessary for the creation of a communal society. In all probability, the proletarian revolution will transform existing society gradually and will be able to abolish private property only when the means of production are available in sufficient quantity.
annotation.summary: Private property cannot be abolished overnight because the productive forces must first be developed enough.
annotation.explanation: Engels answers the question of abolition at one stroke by saying the proletarian revolution will transform society gradually and abolish private property only when the means of production exist in sufficient quantity.
annotation.context: The answer anticipates the later distinction between lower and higher phases of communist society.

annotation.targetText: The middle bourgeoisie, by which is meant chiefly the national bourgeoisie, [3] is inconsistent in its attitude towards the Chinese revolution: they feel the need for revolution and favour the revolutionary movement against imperialism and the warlords when they are smarting under the blows of foreign capital and the oppression of the warlords, but they become suspicious of the revolution when they sense that, with the militant participation of the proletariat at home and the active support of the international proletariat abroad, the revolution is threatening the hope of their class to attain the status of a big bourgeoisie.
annotation.summary: The national bourgeoisie in semi-colonial nations is caught in a contradiction: it resents foreign imperialist domination but fears working-class militancy.
annotation.explanation: Mao formulates the classic Marxist analysis of the dual character of the national bourgeoisie in semi-colonial countries. Because foreign monopolies restrict their domestic market, national capitalists intermittently support anti-imperialist struggles; however, because they themselves exploit wage labor, they panic whenever working-class and peasant organization threatens private property, causing their right wing to defect to imperialism (as Chiang Kai-shek did in the 1927 Shanghai massacre).
annotation.context: Domestic manufacturing owners in developing countries often support state tariffs against foreign imports, yet quickly ally with right-wing coups or IMF austerity programs when domestic workers strike for higher wages.

annotation.targetText: Some say that Leninism is the application of Marxism to the conditions that are peculiar to the situation in Russia. This definition contains a particle of truth, but not the whole truth by any means. Lenin, indeed, applied Marxism to Russian conditions, and applied it in a masterly way. But if Leninism were only the application of Marxism to the conditions that are peculiar to Russia it would be a purely national and only a national, a purely Russian and only a Russian, phenomenon. We know, however, that Leninism is not merely a Russian, but an international phenomenon rooted in the whole of international development.
annotation.summary: Leninism is an international theoretical system rooted in global imperialist development.
annotation.explanation: Refutes the opportunist claim that Leninism was uniquely tailored for backward Russian conditions. While Lenin applied Marxism masterfully to Russian reality, the core problems he resolved (imperialist war, monopoly trusts, the vanguard party, national liberation) belong to the entire world capitalist system.

annotation.targetText: The first contradiction is the contradiction between labour and capital. Imperialism is the omnipotence of the monopolist trusts and syndicates, of the banks and the financial oligarchy, in the industrial countries. In the fight against this omnipotence, the customary methods of the working class: trade unions and cooperatives, parliamentary parties and the parliamentary struggle: have proved to be totally inadequate. Either place yourself at the mercy of capital, eke out a wretched existence as of old and sink lower and lower, or adopt a new weapon: this is the alternative imperialism puts before the vast masses of the proletariat. Imperialism brings the working class to revolution.
annotation.summary: Imperialist monopoly capital intensifies class exploitation beyond the capacity of legal trade unionism.
annotation.explanation: Under monopoly capitalism, the financial oligarchy and giant corporate syndicates concentrate economic power to an extreme degree. Peaceful, reformist parliamentary methods and legal trade union negotiations become completely inadequate to defend working-class survival, leaving socialist revolution as the only viable path forward.

annotation.targetText: The scientific significance of N.I. Bukharin's work consists particularly in this, that he examines the fundamental facts of world economy relating to imperialism as a whole, as a definite stage in the growth of most highly developed capitalism.
annotation.summary: Lenin highlights that imperialism must be analyzed scientifically as a definite historical stage of highly developed monopoly capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Rather than treating imperialism as a reversible diplomatic policy choice or a moral insult, Marxism analyzes it as the necessary economic stage reached when free competition gives way to monopoly.

annotation.targetText: The typical ruler of the world became finance capital, a power that is peculiarly mobile and flexible, peculiarly intertwined at home and internationally, peculiarly devoid of individuality and divorced from the immediate processes of production, peculiarly easy to concentrate, a power that has already made peculiarly large strides on the road of concentration, so that literally several hundred billionaires and millionaires hold in their hands the fate of the whole world.
annotation.summary: Finance capital concentrates global economic and political power into the hands of a few hundred financial oligarchs.
annotation.explanation: Lenin describes how the fusion of banking and industrial capital creates a hyper-mobile financial oligarchy divorced from direct production yet commanding the fate of nations.

annotation.targetText: There is no doubt that the development is going in the direction of a single world trust that will swallow up all enterprises and all states without exception. But the development in this direction is proceeding under such stress, with such a tempo, with such contradictions, conflicts, and convulsions-not only economical, but also political, national, etc., etc.-that before a single world trust will be reached, before the respective national finance capitals will have formed a world union of "ultra-imperialism," imperialism will inevitably explode, capitalism will turn into its opposite.
annotation.summary: Before global capitalism could ever unite into Kautsky's peaceful 'single world trust', its violent contradictions will cause imperialism to explode in socialist revolution.
annotation.explanation: Lenin refutes Karl Kautsky's reformist dream of 'ultra-imperialism', demonstrating that the uneven, catastrophic development of monopoly capitalism intensifies wars and class struggles long before a global monopoly could peacefully consolidate.

annotation.targetText: World finance capitalism and the internationally organised domination of the banks are one of the undeniable facts of economic reality.
annotation.summary: International banking syndicates and finance capital stretch their tentacles across every continent and industry.
annotation.explanation: Behind industrial cartels stand giant banks that finance colonial railways, mines, plantations, and armaments, fusing banking and industrial capital on a world scale.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. III: Organisation Forms of World Economy

annotation.targetText: The conditions of direct exploitation and those of the realisation of surplus value are not identical. They are separated logically as well as by time and space. The first are only limited by the productive power of society, the last by the proportional relations of the various lines of production and by the consuming power of society.
annotation.summary: Quoting Marx's Capital Vol. 3, Bukharin explains how depressed working-class consumption forces monopolies to seek foreign sales markets.
annotation.explanation: Because capitalism restricts the purchasing power of the domestic working masses while expanding mass production, monopolies are driven to dump surplus commodities abroad and annex colonial markets.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. V: World Sales Markets and Changed Sales Conditions

annotation.targetText: We have in mind the disproportion between the development of industry and the development of agriculture as a source of raw material for the manufacturing industry.
annotation.summary: The lagging development of agriculture behind rapid industrial growth triggers a global scramble among monopolies to seize raw material sources.
annotation.explanation: Because monopoly ownership of land holds back agricultural output while manufacturing demand for cotton, rubber, timber, and ores skyrockets, imperialist powers fight to monopolize colonial raw material supplies.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. VI: World Market for Raw Materials, and Change in the Conditions of Purchasing Materials

annotation.targetText: For monopoly organisations can overcome the tendency towards lowering the rate of profit by receiving monopoly superprofits at the expense of the non-trustified industries. Out of the surplus value created every year, one portion, that which has been created in the nontrustified branches of industry, is being transferred to the coowners of capitalist monopolies, whereas the share of the outsiders continually decreases. Thus the entire process drives capital beyond the frontiers of the country.
annotation.summary: Cartels and trusts restrict domestic investment to maintain monopoly superprofits, driving overaccumulated capital to seek higher returns abroad.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin explains the economic compulsion behind capital export: monopoly cartels limit domestic output to keep prices high and export their surplus capital to colonies and foreign markets.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. VII: World Movement of Capital, and Change in the Economic Forms of International Connections

annotation.targetText:
We have laid bare three fundamental motives for the conquest policies of modern capitalist states: increased competition in the sales markets, in the markets of raw materials, and for the spheres of capital investment. This is what the modern development of capitalism and its transformation into finance capitalism has brought about.

Those three roots of the policy of finance capitalism, however, represent in substance only three facets of the same phenomenon, namely of the conflict between the growth of productive forces on the one hand, and the "national" limits of the production organisation on the other.
annotation.summary: The three drivers of imperialist conquest (sales markets, raw materials, and capital investment spheres) stem from the conflict between global productive forces and national bourgeois states.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin synthesizes his theory of imperialism: productive forces have outgrown the narrow framework of the nation-state, forcing finance capital to attempt to resolve the contradiction through military conquest.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. VIII: World Economy and the "National" State

annotation.targetText: It is perfectly obvious that not races but state organisations of definite groups of the bourgeoisie are conducting the struggle. It is also perfectly obvious that one or the other grouping of the great powers is determined, not by a community of certain racial tasks, but by a community of capitalist aims at a given moment.
annotation.summary: Bukharin demolishes racial theories of imperialism, showing that military alliances follow capitalist profit interests rather than racial identity.
annotation.explanation: Pointing to multi-ethnic war coalitions and shifting alliances among European and Asian powers, Bukharin exposes racial ideology as a ruling-class fabrication designed to mask the war aims of finance capital.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. IX: Imperialism as an Historic Category

annotation.targetText: By concentration we understand the increase of capital that is due to the capitalisation of the surplus value produced by that capital; under centralisation we understand the joining together of various individual capital units which thus form a new larger unit.
annotation.summary: Concentration grows capital through reinvesting surplus value, while centralization merges existing capitals into giant trusts and state-capitalist blocs.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin applies Marx's laws of concentration and centralization to the world economy, showing how national economies coalesce into competing 'state-capitalist trusts' that wage war to centralize territory.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. X: Reproduction of the Process of Concentration and Centralisation on a World Scale

annotation.targetText: The growth of competition outlined in the last chapter reduces itself to the fact that the continuous elimination of competition among smaller economic units calls forth a sharper competition among large economic units.
annotation.summary: Eliminating competition among small firms inside a nation intensifies destructive competition among giant state-capitalist trusts on the world stage.
annotation.explanation: Instead of competing merely through lower prices, state-capitalist trusts deploy tariffs, credit blockades, raw material boycotts, and military force to crush foreign rivals.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. XI: Means of Competitive Struggle, and State Power

annotation.targetText: Together with a truly barbarous squandering of production forces, with the destruction of the material means of production and of the living labour power, together with the devitalisation of economy through monstrous socially harmful expenditures, the war, like a gigantic crisis, has intensified the fundamental tendencies of capitalist development; it has hastened to an extraordinary degree the growth of finance capitalist relations and the centralisation of capital on a world scale.
annotation.summary: Imperialist world war acts as a gigantic crisis that destroys productive forces while vastly accelerating finance-capitalist centralization and state capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin documents how World War I wiped out small enterprises, subordinated entire national economies to state-capitalist war syndicates, and propelled the United States to global financial supremacy.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. XIII: War and Economic Evolution

annotation.targetText: For the collapse of the proletarian movement is a result of the unequal situation of the "state capitalist trusts" within the boundaries of world economy. Just as it is impossible to understand modern capitalism and its imperialist policy without analysing the tendencies of world capitalism, so the basic tendencies in the proletarian movement cannot be understood without analysing world capitalism.
annotation.summary: The 1914 betrayal of the Second International stemmed from the privileged position of imperialist state-capitalist trusts in the world economy.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin shows how superprofits from colonial exploitation allowed metropolitan capitalists to cultivate a reformist labor aristocracy that temporarily identified its interests with its own imperialist state.

annotation.summary: Socialism is not an idealist figment of the imagination, but the working class's practical appropriation and mastery of large-scale organization created by capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Against the idealist fantasy that socialism can be invented out of pure revolutionary willpower without technical expertise, Lenin insists that the proletarian state must employ and learn from first-class technical specialists under workers' oversight.

annotation.targetText: As a matter of fact, freedom and democracy exist not in the abstract, but only in the concrete. annotation.summary: The dictatorship of the proletariat represents the democratic rule of the armed working class, modeled on the Paris Commune.
annotation.explanation: Rebuts the anarchist charge that Marxist dictatorship means rule by a few elite bureaucrats. Citing Engels and the Paris Commune, Stalin demonstrates that the proletarian dictatorship is the organized self-defense and governance of the armed working class over the defeated exploiters.
annotation.context: Following the defeat of the 1871 Paris Commune, bourgeois commentators and anarchists attacked the concept of proletarian dictatorship, prompting Marx and Engels to point to the Commune's direct democracy as its historical living model.

annotation.targetText: first step in the revolution by the working class is to raise the proletariat to the position of ruling class, to win the battle of democracy. The proletariat will use its political supremacy to wrest, by degrees, all capital from the bourgeoisie, to centralise all instruments of production in the hands of the State, i.e., of the proletariat organised as the ruling class;
annotation.summary: The first task of a workers' revolution is to win political power as a class and use the state to take over the means of production.

annotation.targetText: The first contradiction is the contradiction between labour and capital. Imperialism is the omnipotence of the monopolist trusts and syndicates, of the banks and the financial oligarchy, in the industrial countries. In the fight against this omnipotence, the customary methods of the working class: trade unions and cooperatives, parliamentary parties and the parliamentary struggle: have proved to be totally inadequate. Either place yourself at the mercy of capital, eke out a wretched existence as of old and sink lower and lower, or adopt a new weapon: this is the alternative imperialism puts before the vast masses of the proletariat. Imperialism brings the working class to revolution.
annotation.summary: Imperialist monopoly capital intensifies class exploitation beyond the capacity of legal trade unionism.
annotation.explanation: Under monopoly capitalism, the financial oligarchy and giant corporate syndicates concentrate economic power to an extreme degree. Peaceful, reformist parliamentary methods and legal trade union negotiations become completely inadequate to defend working-class survival, leaving socialist revolution as the only viable path forward.

annotations.chapterTitle: I. The Historical Roots of Leninism

annotation.targetText: Firstly, the testing of the theoretical dogmas of the Second International in the crucible of the revolutionary struggle of the masses, in the crucible of living practice: that is to say, the restoration of the broken unity between theory and practice, the healing of the rift between them; for only in this way can a truly proletarian party armed with revolutionary theory be created.
annotation.summary: Leninism restores the unity of theory and practice against Second International dogmatism.
annotation.explanation: The Second International reduced Marxism to dry, academic formulas and parliamentary routine divorced from actual revolutionary struggle. Lenin re-established the vital link between theoretical science and mass action, insisting that all dogma must be tested and forged in the living furnace of practical mass revolution.
annotation.context: In August 1914, the dominant leaders of the Second International abandoned anti-militarist resolutions to vote for national war credits in World War I, prompting Lenin to break irrevocably with their reformist opportunism.

annotation.targetText: dictatorship of the proletariat is not a mere change of personalities in the government, a change of the cabinet," etc., leaving the old economic and political order intact.
annotation.summary: The dictatorship of the proletariat requires smashing the bourgeois state, not a mere change of cabinet.
annotation.explanation: Socialist revolution cannot simply inherit existing capitalist parliaments, courts, and police bureaucracies. The working class must smash the old state machine and erect a new proletarian state capable of expropriating the capitalists and defending workers power.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.summary: The goal of workers is not to make the state free but to subordinate it to society.
annotation.explanation: Marx mocks the demand for a 'free state'. In an empire that is almost as unfree as Russia, freedom consists in converting the state from an organ standing above society into one completely subordinate to it.
annotation.context: The passage feeds into the later theory of the workers' state and its eventual withering away.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.explanation: Writing during the Kulturkampf, Marx says liberal 'freedom of conscience' should simply mean freedom from police interference in matters of belief, while the workers' party should show it wants to free conscience from religious delusion.
annotation.context: Lenin used this passage to argue that religion is a private matter as far as the state is concerned, but not as far as the party is concerned.

annotation.explanation: Marx criticises the draft for ignoring the revolutionary transformation between capitalism and communism. Universal suffrage, direct legislation and a militia are old liberal slogans that do not address the question of what kind of state the proletariat needs.

This article will express our views on guerrilla warfare and its correct
utilization. Above all, we must emphasize at the outset that this form of
struggle is a means to an end. That end, essential and inevitable for any
revolutionary, is the conquest of political power.
annotation.summary: Guerrilla warfare is not an end in itself, but an instrument for the revolutionary conquest of political power.
annotation.explanation: Guerrilla fighting is neither a romantic adventure nor a self-sufficient military objective. It is a specific political method of armed struggle employed by an oppressed people to destroy the repressive state apparatus of the ruling class and establish revolutionary workers and peasants power.

annotation.targetText:
Socialism is divided into three main trends : reformism, anarchism and Marxism.

Reformism (Bernstein and others), which regards socialism as a remote goal and 
nothing more, reformism, which actually repudiates the socialist revolution and 
aims at establishing socialism by peaceful means, reformism, which advocates not 
class struggle but class collaboration : this reformism is decaying day by day, is 
day by day losing all semblance of socialism and, in our opinion, it is totally 
unnecessary to examine it in these articles when defining socialism.

It is altogether different with Marxism and anarchism: both are at the present 
time recognised as socialist trends, they are waging a fierce struggle against each 
other, both are trying to present themselves to the proletariat as genuinely socialist 
doctrines, and, of course, a study and comparison of the two will be far more interesting 
for the reader.

We are not the kind of people who, when the word "anarchism" is mentioned, turn 
away contemptuously and say with a supercilious wave of the hand: "Why waste time 
on that, it's not worth talking about!" We think that such cheap "criticism" is 
undignified and useless.

Nor are we the kind of people who console themselves with the thought that the 
Anarchists "have no masses behind them and, therefore, are not so dangerous." It 
is not who has a larger or smaller "mass" following today, but the essence of the 
doctrine that matters. If the "doctrine" of the Anarchists expresses the truth, 
then it goes without saying that it will certainly hew a path for itself and will 
rally the masses around itself. If, however, it is unsound and built up on a false 
foundation, it will not last long and will remain suspended in mid-air. But the 
unsoundness of anarchism must be proved.

Some people believe that Marxism and anarchism are based on the same principles 
and that the disagreements between them concern only tactics, so that, in the opinion 
of these people, it is quite impossible to draw a contrast between these two trends.

This is a great mistake.

We believe that the Anarchists are real enemies of Marxism. Accordingly, we also 
hold that a real struggle must be waged against real enemies. Therefore, it is necessary 
to examine the "doctrine" of the Anarchists from beginning to end and weigh it up 
thoroughly from all aspects.
annotation.summary: Distinguishes Marxism from both bourgeois reformism and petty-bourgeois anarchism.
annotation.explanation: Categorizes modern socialism into three distinct currents: reformism (class collaboration and denial of revolution), anarchism (individualist repudiation of the state and class discipline), and Marxism (scientific class struggle culminating in the dictatorship of the proletariat).

annotation.targetText:
The cornerstone of anarchism is the individual, whose emancipation, 
according to its tenets, is the principal condition for the emancipation of the 
masses, the collective body. According to the tenets of anarchism, the emancipation 
of the masses is impossible until the individual is emancipated. Accordingly, its 
slogan is: "Everything for the individual." The cornerstone of Marxism, however, 
is the masses, whose emancipation, according to its tenets, is the principal condition 
for the emancipation of the individual. That is to say, according to the tenets 
of Marxism, the emancipation of the individual is impossible until the masses are 
emancipated. Accordingly, its slogan is: "Everything for the masses."
annotation.summary: Contrasts the individualist premise of anarchism with the collective foundation of scientific socialism.
annotation.explanation: Anarchism places the isolated individual at its center, asserting that social emancipation occurs only after individual liberation. Marxism inverts this premise: individual freedom is materially impossible so long as the mass of humanity remains bound by capitalist exploitation. Genuine individual emancipation requires collective class liberation.

It is altogether different with Marxism and anarchism: both are at the present 
time recognised as socialist trends, they are waging a fierce struggle against each 
other, both are trying to present themselves to the proletariat as genuinely socialist 
doctrines, and, of course, a study and comparison of the two will be far more interesting 
for the reader.

We are not the kind of people who, when the word "anarchism" is mentioned, turn 
away contemptuously and say with a supercilious wave of the hand: "Why waste time 
on that, it's not worth talking about!" We think that such cheap "criticism" is 
undignified and useless.

Nor are we the kind of people who console themselves with the thought that the 
Anarchists "have no masses behind them and, therefore, are not so dangerous." It 
is not who has a larger or smaller "mass" following today, but the essence of the 
doctrine that matters. If the "doctrine" of the Anarchists expresses the truth, 
then it goes without saying that it will certainly hew a path for itself and will 
rally the masses around itself. If, however, it is unsound and built up on a false 
foundation, it will not last long and will remain suspended in mid-air. But the 
unsoundness of anarchism must be proved.

Some people believe that Marxism and anarchism are based on the same principles 
and that the disagreements between them concern only tactics, so that, in the opinion 
of these people, it is quite impossible to draw a contrast between these two trends.

This is a great mistake.

We believe that the Anarchists are real enemies of Marxism. Accordingly, we also 
hold that a real struggle must be waged against real enemies. Therefore, it is necessary 
to examine the "doctrine" of the Anarchists from beginning to end and weigh it up 
thoroughly from all aspects.
annotation.summary: Distinguishes Marxism from both bourgeois reformism and petty-bourgeois anarchism.
annotation.explanation: Categorizes modern socialism into three distinct currents: reformism (class collaboration and denial of revolution), anarchism (individualist repudiation of the state and class discipline), and Marxism (scientific class struggle culminating in the dictatorship of the proletariat).

annotation.summary: The dictatorship of the proletariat represents the democratic rule of the armed working class, modeled on the Paris Commune.

annotation.targetText: Yesterday, the main task of the moment was, as determinedly as possible, to nationalise, confiscate, beat down and crush the bourgeoisie, and put down sabotage. Today, only a blind man could fail to see that we have nationalised, confiscated, beaten down and put down more than we have had time to count. The difference between socialisation and simple confiscation is that confiscation can be carried out by “determination” alone, without the ability to calculate and distribute properly, whereas socialisation cannot be brought about without this ability.
annotation.summary: Confiscation requires only political determination, whereas genuine socialization requires the organizational capacity to calculate, account for, and distribute production.
annotation.explanation: Lenin refutes the ultra-left illusion that decreeing further nationalizations automatically creates socialism; real socialization demands nationwide accounting, administration, and disciplined economic coordination.

annotation.targetText: It is not state capitalism that is at war with socialism, but the petty bourgeoisie plus private capitalism fighting together against both state capitalism and socialism. This is an absolutely unquestionable fact of reality, and the root of the economic mistake of the “Left Communists” is that they have failed to understand it.
annotation.summary: In a predominantly small-peasant economy, the primary internal threat to socialism is petty-bourgeois profiteering and resistance to state accounting, not state capitalism.
annotation.explanation: By attacking 'state capitalism' in 1918, the Left Communists inadvertently aided small-proprietor grain speculators and private black-marketeers who opposed all state regulation and accounting.

annotation.targetText: At present, petty-bourgeois capitalism prevails in Russia, and it is one and the same road that leads from it to both large-scale state capitalism and to socialism, through one and the same intermediary station called “national accounting and control of production and distribution”. Those who fail to understand this are committing an unpardonable mistake in economics. Either they do not know the facts of life, do not see what actually exists and are unable to look the truth in the face, or they confine themselves to abstractly comparing “capitalism” with “socialism” and fail to study the concrete forms and stages of the transition that is taking place in our country.
annotation.summary: Abstractly counterposing 'capitalism' and 'socialism' ignores the concrete material intermediary stages required to transition from small-scale production to socialism.
annotation.explanation: Lenin critiques the idealist method of the Left Communists, who compare abstract concepts of capitalism and socialism in their heads instead of studying the real material pathway of national accounting and control.

annotation.targetText: Law, morality, religion, are to him so many bourgeois prejudices, behind which lurk in ambush just as many bourgeois interests.

annotation.targetText: The ideas of religious liberty and freedom of conscience merely gave expression to the sway of free competition within the domain of knowledge.
annotation.summary: Even religious freedom is treated as an expression of capitalist free competition applied to ideas.
annotation.explanation: Marx and Engels argue that ideas change with material conditions. The rise of the bourgeoisie produced demands for religious toleration and freedom of conscience, which mirror free competition in the market, and a different economic base will produce different ideas.

annotation.targetText: But Communism abolishes eternal truths, it abolishes all religion, and all morality, instead of constituting them on a new basis; it therefore acts in contradiction to all past historical experience.
annotation.summary: The charge that communism destroys religion and morality is answered by pointing out that all past ideas were shaped by class antagonism.
annotation.explanation: Marx and Engels turn the accusation around: since all past society moved through class antagonisms, the ideas of every age share common forms. Communism breaks with traditional property relations and therefore with traditional ideas.
annotation.context: This is one of the clearest statements that Marxism treats morality and religion as historical products rather than timeless absolutes.

annotation.targetText: The religious reflex of the real world can, in any case, only then finally vanish, when the practical relations of every-day life offer to man none but perfectly intelligible and reasonable relations with regard to his fellowmen and to Nature.

annotation.explanation: Marx treats religion as a reflection of real alienated social life. As long as the relations between people appear as relations between things governed by market forces, mystical forms of thought persist, so changing material relations is the real route to ending religious illusion.
annotation.context: The passage sits in the section on commodity fetishism and is often paired with the 'opium of the people' line as Marx's theory of religion.

annotation.explanation: Marx and Engels define the state through its class function. When class distinctions vanish and production is concentrated in the hands of the associated nation, public power loses its political character, anticipating the later idea of the withering away of the state.
annotation.context: Lenin quoted this passage in The State and Revolution to argue that a workers' state is a transitional form that prepares its own disappearance.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.targetText: In place of the old bourgeois society, with its classes and class antagonisms, we shall have an association, in which the free development of each is the condition for the free development of all.
annotation.summary: Communist society replaces class antagonism with an association where each person's freedom depends on the freedom of everyone.
annotation.explanation: This sentence states the humanist goal of the whole programme. Abolishing private ownership of the means of production is not an end in itself but the precondition for individual development that is no longer bought at the expense of other classes.
annotation.context: It is frequently cited against the claim that Marxism seeks to submerge the individual in the collective.

annotation.targetText: first step in the revolution by the working class is to raise the proletariat to the position of ruling class, to win the battle of democracy. The proletariat will use its political supremacy to wrest, by degrees, all capital from the bourgeoisie, to centralise all instruments of production in the hands of the State, i.e., of the proletariat organised as the ruling class;
annotation.summary: The first task of a workers' revolution is to win political power as a class and use the state to take over the means of production.
annotation.explanation: Here the Manifesto links democracy with proletarian rule: winning the battle of democracy means the majority class organised as the ruling class, then centralising capital in its hands. This is the seed of the later theory of the dictatorship of the proletariat.
annotation.context: The passage directly shapes later debates about whether socialism is reached through elections, insurrection, or a combination of the two.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.targetText: Just as the offensive power of a squadron of cavalry, or the defensive power of a regiment of infantry is essentially different from the sum of the offensive or defensive powers of the individual cavalry or infantry soldiers taken separately, so the sum total of the mechanical forces exerted by isolated workmen differs from the social force that is developed, when many hands take part simultaneously in one and the same undivided operation, such as raising a heavy weight, turning a winch, or removing an obstacle.
annotation.summary: The collective social power of cooperation: combined labour produces a social force greater than the sum of isolated workers.
annotation.explanation: When workers cooperate under a unified plan, their combined collective force generates an enhanced productive power that exceeds the mathematical sum of individual isolated efforts. Under capitalism, this social power of combined labour is appropriated by the capitalist free of charge.
annotation.context: Part IV, Chapter 13: Co-operation

Centralisation of the means of production and
socialisation of labour at last reach a point where they become incompatible
with their capitalist integument. This integument is burst asunder. The
knell of capitalist private property sounds. The expropriators are expropriated.
annotation.summary: The expropriators are expropriated: extreme centralization and socialized production burst the capitalist integument, leading to socialist transformation.
annotation.explanation: Capitalist accumulation leads to extreme centralization and socialized production. Eventually, the monopoly of capital becomes a fetter, leading to the socialist transformation.

annotation.targetText: The capitalist mode of appropriation, the result of the capitalist mode of production, produces capitalist private property. This is the first negation of individual private property, as founded on the labour of the proprietor. But capitalist production begets, with the inexorability of a law of Nature, its own negation. It is the negation of negation. This does not re-establish private property for the producer, but gives him individual property based on the acquisition of the capitalist era: i.e., on cooperation and the possession in common of the land and of the means of production.
annotation.summary: The negation of negation: capitalist socialization culminates in the expropriation of private property in favor of common ownership.
annotation.explanation: Individual private property based on self-earned labour was first negated by capitalist private property (the expropriation of many small producers by few capitalists). In turn, capitalist development inexorably socializes the labour process, leading to the negation of negation: the collective appropriation of the means of production by the associated working class.
annotation.context: Part VIII, Chapter 32: Historical Tendency of Capitalist Accumulation

annotation.targetText: At present, petty-bourgeois capitalism prevails in Russia, and it is one and the same road that leads from it to both large-scale state capitalism and to socialism, through one and the same intermediary station called “national accounting and control of production and distribution”. Those who fail to understand this are committing an unpardonable mistake in economics. Either they do not know the facts of life, do not see what actually exists and are unable to look the truth in the face, or they confine themselves to abstractly comparing “capitalism” with “socialism” and fail to study the concrete forms and stages of the transition that is taking place in our country.

annotation.targetText: We are confronted with two types of social contradictions : those between ourselves and the enemy and those among the people. The two are totally different in nature.
annotation.summary: Socialist society faces two fundamentally different kinds of conflicts: antagonistic conflicts between the people and their enemies, and non-antagonistic conflicts among the people themselves.
annotation.explanation: Mao introduces his central theoretical innovation for socialist governance: separating hostile class antagonisms against counter-revolutionaries from internal disagreements and structural tensions among the working masses and their allies.
annotation.context: A socialist state must treat foreign-backed sabotage or armed counter-revolution differently from a workplace dispute or policy disagreement among ordinary workers.

annotation.targetText: The only way to settle questions of an ideological nature or controversial issues among the people is by the democratic method, the method of discussion, criticism, persuasion and education, and not by the method of coercion or repression.
annotation.summary: Ideological questions and debates among the people cannot be solved by force or administrative bans; they can only be resolved through open discussion, criticism, persuasion, and education.
annotation.explanation: Because ideological beliefs and questions of right and wrong among the people cannot be forced by decree, Mao insists on patient reasoning, debate, and the 'unity : criticism : unity' method.
annotation.context: Banning a mistaken viewpoint among workers without explaining why it is wrong only drives the idea underground, whereas open discussion builds genuine understanding.

annotation.explanation: Mao warns that while dogmatists apply Marxist phrases mechanically, revisionists pay lip-service to Marxism while attacking its core principles: materialist dialectics, party leadership, and the people's democratic dictatorship.

annotation.targetText: Man is to have the opportunity to develop himself to the full : that should be the purpose of all human socialisation, which means that he must not be fettered to the soil on which he has been placed by accident of birth.

It is true that the rural and urban petty bourgeoisie 
now constitute the majority and are really poor, but is that the point? The petty 
bourgeoisie has long constituted the majority, but up to now it has displayed no

Their views express, not the future of bourgeois society, which is striding with irresistible force towards the socialisation of labour, but the present and even the past of that society, the domination of blind chance over the scattered and isolated small, producer.
annotation.summary: Lenin unmasks the petty-bourgeois class roots of anarchism: while socialism is rooted in large-scale socialized production and collective discipline, anarchism is an ideology of individualist rebellion reflecting the economic isolation of petty commodity producers.

annotation.targetText: Many petty bourgeois, it is true, did vote for the Cadets. But the class character of a party cannot be judged from the fact that certain elements, among others, voted for it at a given moment.
annotation.summary: Lenin clarifies a fundamental Marxist principle of political sociology: the class nature of a party is defined by the objective material interests of the class that funds and directs it, not by transient electoral cross-voting from confused intermediate strata.

annotation.targetText: The second root of Fascism lies in the retarding of the world revolution by the treacherous attitude of the reformist leaders. Large numbers of the petty bourgeoisie, including even the middle classes, had discarded their war-time psychology for a certain sympathy with reformist socialism, hoping that the latter would bring about a reformation of society along democratic lines. They were disappointed in their hopes.
annotation.summary: Social-democratic betrayal of socialist revolution drives ruined middle strata and disillusioned workers into the arms of fascism.
annotation.explanation: When reformist leaders collaborate with the bourgeoisie instead of overthrowing capitalism, impoverished petty-bourgeois layers and demoralized workers lose faith in socialism and seek refuge in fascist demagogy.

annotation.targetText: Louis Bonaparte took the political power from the capitalists under the pretext of protecting them
annotation.summary: Bonapartism: state executive power claiming independence while safeguarding capitalist exploitation.
annotation.explanation: Engels analyzes how Bonapartism arises when class struggle produces an equilibrium of weakness: the autocratic state appears to rule above classes while expanding capitalist industry and financial speculation.

annotation.targetText: Our enemy, Japan, is first of all a moribund imperialist power; she is already in her era of decline and is not only different from Britain at the time of the subjugation of India, when British capitalism was still in the era of its ascendancy, but also different from what she herself was at the time of World War I twenty years ago.
annotation.summary: Japan cannot repeat Britain's past conquest of India because world imperialism is now in decline while China has a Communist Party, a revolutionary army, and global support.
annotation.explanation: Mao shows why mechanical historical analogies fail: whether a small power can conquer a large country depends on the concrete historical epoch, and 1930s fascist imperialism is in its death throes while anti-colonial revolution is rising.
annotation.context: Defeatists often point to past colonial conquests while ignoring how mass political consciousness and international solidarity have transformed the balance of power.

annotation.targetText: History shows that wars are divided into two kinds, just and unjust. All wars that are progressive are just, and all wars that impede progress are unjust. We Communists oppose all unjust wars that impede progress, but we do not oppose progressive, just wars.
annotation.summary: Marxists distinguish between two types of war: unjust wars of imperialist aggression and oppression, which Communists oppose, and just wars of liberation and progress, which Communists support.
annotation.explanation: Unlike bourgeois pacifism, which condemns all violence in the abstract without examining its class character, Marxism evaluates every war concretely: opposing predatory imperialist wars while actively supporting anti-colonial and revolutionary wars of liberation.
annotation.context: Defending a colonized nation against fascist invasion is fundamentally different from imperialist powers fighting each other to redivide colonies.

annotation.targetText: Fascism is the concentrated expression of the general offensive undertaken by the world bourgeoisie against the proletariat. Its overthrow is therefore an absolute necessity, nay, it is even a question of the every-day existence and of the bread and butter of every ordinary worker.
annotation.summary: Fascism is the concentrated offensive of big capital against the working class and its daily survival.
annotation.explanation: Zetkin establishes that fascism is not an isolated political aberration, but the generalized offensive of the capitalist ruling class to crush working-class living standards and organizations.

annotation.targetText: Fascism, on the contrary, viewed objectively, is not the revenge of the bourgeoisie in retaliation for proletarian aggression against the bourgeoisie, but it is a punishment of the proletariat for failing to carry on the revolution begun in Russia. The Fascist leaders are not a small and exclusive caste; they extend deeply into wide elements of the population.
annotation.summary: Unlike a narrow military junta, fascism is a mass movement that punishes the working class for an uncompleted socialist revolution.
annotation.explanation: Contrasting Mussolini's movement with Admiral Horthy's officer clique in Hungary, Zetkin explains that fascism builds a broad social base among displaced layers of society when reformist betrayal stalls proletarian revolution.

annotation.targetText: Fascism, with all its forcefulness in the prosecution of its violent deeds, is indeed nothing else but the expression of the disintegration and decay of capitalist economy, and the symptom of the dissolution of the bourgeois State.
annotation.summary: Fascist violence is not a sign of capitalist vitality, but a symptom of capitalist economic decay and state crisis.
annotation.explanation: Where social-democratic reformists cowered before the supposed invulnerability of the bourgeoisie, Zetkin shows that the ruling class turns to fascism precisely because normal parliamentary institutions and capitalist economics are breaking down.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.targetText: The second root of Fascism lies in the retarding of the world revolution by the treacherous attitude of the reformist leaders. Large numbers of the petty bourgeoisie, including even the middle classes, had discarded their war-time psychology for a certain sympathy with reformist socialism, hoping that the latter would bring about a reformation of society along democratic lines. They were disappointed in their hopes.
annotation.summary: Social-democratic betrayal of socialist revolution drives ruined middle strata and disillusioned workers into the arms of fascism.
annotation.explanation: When reformist leaders collaborate with the bourgeoisie instead of overthrowing capitalism, impoverished petty-bourgeois layers and demoralized workers lose faith in socialism and seek refuge in fascist demagogy.

annotation.targetText: Fascism has diverse characteristics in different countries. Nevertheless it has two distinguishing features in all countries, namely, the pretence of a revolutionary programme, which is cleverly adapted to the interests and demands of the large masses, and, on the other hand, the application of the most brutal violence.
annotation.summary: The dual weapon of fascism everywhere: pseudo-revolutionary anti-capitalist demagogy combined with brutal anti-worker terror.
annotation.explanation: Zetkin identifies the universal formula of fascism: it wins mass support by mimicking anti-elitist, revolutionary slogans appealing to ruined lower classes, while deploying paramilitary terror squads against organized labor.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.targetText: The Fascist Party created a double-edged weapon for the corruption and terrorisation of the working class. For the corruption of the working class the Fascist Trade Unions were created, the so-called corporations in which workers and employers were united. To terrorise the working class, the Fascist Party created the militant squads which had grown out of the punitive expeditions.
annotation.summary: Fascist corporatism corrupts labor through class-collaborationist unions while Blackshirt squads terrorize independent workers.
annotation.explanation: In Italy, Mussolini paired Yellow "corporations" (uniting bosses and workers to suppress strikes) with armed paramilitary squads funded by industrialists and landlords to smash revolutionary unions.

annotation.targetText: The destruction of the trade unions has enabled the employers to effect wage reductions of 20 to 30 per cent, and in some cases of even 50 to 60 per cent.
annotation.summary: Once in power, fascism immediately abandons its social promises and enforces massive wage cuts and privatization for big capital.
annotation.explanation: Zetkin documents Mussolini's actual economic record in office: dismantling the eight-hour day, outlawing factory councils, slashing wages by up to 60 percent, abolishing luxury and capital taxes on the rich, and raising indirect taxes on workers.

annotation.targetText: The Third International is, in contradistinction to the old International, an International of all races without any distinctions whatever.
annotation.summary: Zetkin affirms that the Communist International unites working people of all races without any racial hierarchy or colonial chauvinism.
annotation.explanation: Contrasting the Comintern with the European-chauvinist Second International (which tolerated colonialism), Zetkin emphasizes that revolutionary communism is built on uncompromising racial equality and global anti-imperialist solidarity.

annotation.targetText: The Communist Parties must not only be the vanguard of the proletarian manual workers, but also the energetic defenders of the interests of the brain workers. They must be the leaders of all sections of society which are driven into opposition to bourgeois domination because of their interests and their expectations of the future.
annotation.summary: To defeat fascism ideologically, Communist Parties must lead manual workers, intellectual workers, and small peasants alike.
annotation.explanation: Zetkin argues that communists cannot allow fascism to monopolize ruined intellectuals, civil servants, and small peasants; the Party must champion all strata crushed by monopoly capital under the banner of a Workers' and Peasants' Government.

annotation.targetText: The proletariat must have a well organised apparatus of self-defence. Whenever Fascism uses violence, it must be met with proletarian violence. I do not mean by this individual terrorist acts, but the violence of the organised revolutionary class struggle of the proletariat. Germany has made a beginning by organising factory "hundreds." This struggle can only be successful if there is a proletarian united front. The workers must unite for this struggle regardless of party.
annotation.summary: Defeating fascism requires a Proletarian United Front across party lines and organized armed working-class self-defense.
annotation.explanation: Rejecting both passive parliamentary appeals and isolated individual terrorism, Zetkin calls for an all-worker United Front and organized workplace defense squads (factory "hundreds") to crush fascist paramilitaries and overthrow capitalism.

annotation.targetText:
The cornerstone of anarchism is the individual, whose emancipation, 
according to its tenets, is the principal condition for the emancipation of the 
masses, the collective body. According to the tenets of anarchism, the emancipation 
of the masses is impossible until the individual is emancipated. Accordingly, its 
slogan is: "Everything for the individual." The cornerstone of Marxism, however, 
is the masses, whose emancipation, according to its tenets, is the principal condition 
for the emancipation of the individual. That is to say, according to the tenets 
of Marxism, the emancipation of the individual is impossible until the masses are 
emancipated. Accordingly, its slogan is: "Everything for the masses."
annotation.summary: Contrasts the individualist premise of anarchism with the collective foundation of scientific socialism.
annotation.explanation: Anarchism places the isolated individual at its center, asserting that social emancipation occurs only after individual liberation. Marxism inverts this premise: individual freedom is materially impossible so long as the mass of humanity remains bound by capitalist exploitation. Genuine individual emancipation requires collective class liberation.
annotation.context: Written in Tiflis between late 1906 and early 1907 during the reactionary aftermath of the 1905 Russian Revolution, when Georgian anarchist groups under V. Cherkezishvili were winning influence among Caucasian workers.

annotation.targetText:
Socialism is divided into three main trends : reformism, anarchism and Marxism.

Reformism (Bernstein and others), which regards socialism as a remote goal and 
nothing more, reformism, which actually repudiates the socialist revolution and 
aims at establishing socialism by peaceful means, reformism, which advocates not 
class struggle but class collaboration : this reformism is decaying day by day, is 
day by day losing all semblance of socialism and, in our opinion, it is totally 
unnecessary to examine it in these articles when defining socialism.

It is altogether different with Marxism and anarchism: both are at the present 
time recognised as socialist trends, they are waging a fierce struggle against each 
other, both are trying to present themselves to the proletariat as genuinely socialist 
doctrines, and, of course, a study and comparison of the two will be far more interesting 
for the reader.

We are not the kind of people who, when the word "anarchism" is mentioned, turn 
away contemptuously and say with a supercilious wave of the hand: "Why waste time 
on that, it's not worth talking about!" We think that such cheap "criticism" is 
undignified and useless.

Nor are we the kind of people who console themselves with the thought that the 
Anarchists "have no masses behind them and, therefore, are not so dangerous." It 
is not who has a larger or smaller "mass" following today, but the essence of the 
doctrine that matters. If the "doctrine" of the Anarchists expresses the truth, 
then it goes without saying that it will certainly hew a path for itself and will 
rally the masses around itself. If, however, it is unsound and built up on a false 
foundation, it will not last long and will remain suspended in mid-air. But the 
unsoundness of anarchism must be proved.

Some people believe that Marxism and anarchism are based on the same principles 
and that the disagreements between them concern only tactics, so that, in the opinion 
of these people, it is quite impossible to draw a contrast between these two trends.

This is a great mistake.

We believe that the Anarchists are real enemies of Marxism. Accordingly, we also 
hold that a real struggle must be waged against real enemies. Therefore, it is necessary 
to examine the "doctrine" of the Anarchists from beginning to end and weigh it up 
thoroughly from all aspects.
annotation.summary: Distinguishes Marxism from both bourgeois reformism and petty-bourgeois anarchism.
annotation.explanation: Categorizes modern socialism into three distinct currents: reformism (class collaboration and denial of revolution), anarchism (individualist repudiation of the state and class discipline), and Marxism (scientific class struggle culminating in the dictatorship of the proletariat).
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.targetText: Individualism, in the form of the individual action of a person alone in a social milieu, must disappear in Cuba. In the future individualism ought to be the efficient utilization of the whole individual for the absolute benefit of a collectivity.
annotation.summary: Che distinguishes between bourgeois individualism (isolated, competitive careerism) and socialist individuality (the full flourishing of personal talents harmonized with and dedicated to the collective community).
annotation.explanation: Che distinguishes between bourgeois individualism (isolated, competitive careerism) and socialist individuality (the full flourishing of personal talents harmonized with and dedicated to the collective community).

annotation.targetText: The class struggle between the proletariat and the bourgeoisie, the class struggle between the various political forces, and the class struggle between the proletariat and the bourgeoisie in the ideological field will still be protracted and tortuous and at times even very sharp.
annotation.summary: Even after socialist ownership is established, the ideological and political struggle between the working class and the bourgeoisie remains long, complex, and at times intense.
annotation.explanation: Even after private ownership of industry and land is largely socialized, bourgeois and petty-bourgeois worldviews persist for decades, requiring ongoing ideological struggle so capitalism is not restored.
annotation.context: In socialist countries, old habits of individualism, careerism, and market mentality continue to influence culture and policy long after factories are nationalized.

While a person dies every day during the eight or
more hours in which he or she functions as a commodity, individuals
come to life afterward in their spiritual creations. But this remedy bears the
germs of the same sickness: that of a solitary being seeking harmony with
the world.
annotation.summary: Che analyzes the alienation of wage labour under capitalism: workers experience their work-time as self-annihilation and seek refuge in isolated, private spiritual pursuits, reproducing individualist estrangement.

annotation.targetText:
[Mother-right, matriarchate ; Ed.] In this
work the author advances the following propositions: 

(1) That originally man lived in a state of sexual
promiscuity, to describe which Bachofen uses the mistaken term
"hetaerism"; 

(2) that such promiscuity excludes any certainty of
paternity, and that descent could therefore be reckoned only in the female
line, according to mother-right, and that this was originally the case amongst
all the peoples of antiquity; 

(3) that since women, as mothers, were the only parents of
the younger generation that were known with certainty, they held a position of
such high respect and honor that it became the foundation, in Bachofen's
conception, of a regular rule of women (gynaecocracy); 

(4) that the transition to monogamy, where the woman belonged
to one man exclusively, involved a violation of a primitive religious law (that
is, actually a violation of the traditional right of the other men to this
woman), and that in order to expiate this violation or to purchase indulgence
for it the woman had to surrender herself for a limited period.
annotation.summary: 19th-century scholars falsely assumed that the modern patriarchal family had existed unchanged throughout human history, treating temporary capitalist marriage norms as eternal human nature.
annotation.explanation: 19th-century scholars falsely assumed that the modern patriarchal family had existed unchanged throughout human history, treating temporary capitalist marriage norms as eternal human nature.
annotation.context: Engels critiques bourgeois ideology for projecting modern capitalist family structures backward into prehistory. In reality, human family systems evolved dramatically across different economic stages.
